discussion_comments.comment_body:
This dereferences c.Value directly, but ConsumeCounter is value-or-valueFrom (exactly one), so c.Value is nil for a valueFrom entry. The Add on the found path just below already uses ptr.Deref for the same field.

Incubating is selected when PartitionableDevices and ConsumableCapacity are on and SharedConsumableCapacity is off, and dropDisabledDRASharedConsumableCapacityFields keeps an existing valueFrom entry on update. So an object stored while the gate was on can reach here after the gate is off (downgrade or skew), and the deref panics.

ptr.Deref would stop the panic, but incubating doesn't resolve valueFrom, so a zero would under-count; filtering these out in GatherPools while the gate is off may be cleaner. Your call. A gate-off test with PartitionableDevices and ConsumableCapacity still on, plus a persisted valueFrom entry, would cover it.

Fixed by filtering slices containing valueFrom consumption in GatherPools when DRASharedConsumableCapacity is disabled. This leaves the affected pool incomplete and prevents new allocations whose counter usage cannot be accounted for safely.

The filtering covers both initial gathering and the fallback that collects slices from other nodes, consistently across allocator variants.

Added gate-off regressions covering existing valueFrom definitions, allocated and unallocated devices, and devices on another node. A separate static-only pool remains allocatable.
